title: Smoky Beef Bowls
shortDescription: Game-night skillet the whole hall shares
subtitle: Game-night skillet the whole hall shares
description: Game-night skillet the whole hall shares. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoky Beef Bowls in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown beef and onion
steps.instruction: In a 12-inch cast iron skillet over medium-high, brown ground beef with diced onion until no pink remains. Drain grease. Add taco seasoning and ⅓ cup water; simmer until thick. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Layer chips and cheese
steps.instruction: Off heat, scatter tortilla chips over the beef in the skillet. Top with black beans, shredded cheddar, and jalapeños. Target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake at 425°F 8–10 minutes until cheese is fully melted and edges bubble. Watch the broiler side — cast iron holds heat and can burn chip edges fast.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Smoky Beef Bowls onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve from the skillet
steps.instruction: Set the hot skillet on a trivet at the table with sour cream and salsa on the side. Loaded Nacho Skillet is communal — provide a big spoon and expect fingers.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Smoky Beef Bowls — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Label every topping bowl — rookies grab faster when they can read the line.
Keep hot bases (potatoes, chips) in cambros at 200°F and cold toppings on ice if service runs long.
Put forks, napkins, and a trash can at the end of the bar — self-serve feeds get messy fast.
Line up Loaded Nacho Skillet on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Game-night skillet the whole hall shares. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Smoky Beef Bowls runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
